mainTopic: Finishing the ברייתא about a lost חטאת, רבא's rulings on מעילה and leftover money, and the משנה on when items burned entirely on the מזבח become subject to מעילה, פסול, נותר, טמא and פיגול
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the first half of a ברייתא about a lost חטאת follows רבי שמעון, and the second half follows רבנן. A tradition from אביי backs up this split. Next, רבא says everyone agrees there is no מעילה for benefiting from impure meat of קדשי קדשים before זריקה, or from the אימורין of קדשים קלים once they are on the altar. A leftover מצוה to burn them or turn them on the fire does not make them subject to מעילה. רבא then rules that the money goes to ים המלח only if the person learned of his מעילה before his כפרה. If he learned after, the money goes to נדבה, because we never set money aside just to destroy it. A new משנה follows. מעילה applies to items that go entirely to the מזבח, like the קומץ, לבונה and קטורת, from the moment they are declared holy. Once they are placed in a כלי שרת, they can become פסול and carry liability for נותר and טמא, but not for פיגול. The משנה ends with a general rule: items that have מתירין carry these liabilities only after the מתירין are offered, while items without מתירין carry them as soon as they enter the vessel, and פיגול never applies to them.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא follows רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the second half of the ברייתא follows the view of רבנן. The punctuation shows surprise that one ברייתא would be split between two opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the latter clause follows רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from just before this point: the first half of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, and the second half follows רבנן. The "?!" shows that splitting one ברייתא between two opinions sounds surprising, and that sets up the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we try to read a whole ברייתא as following one opinion. Splitting it between רבי שמעון and רבנן is a stretched answer. That is why the גמרא will now bring backing for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter (second) clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The Sages, the majority view that disagrees with an individual sage

phrases.english: And the latter clause follows the Rabbis?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous section of the daf
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא should follow one opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The first half follows רבי שמעון and the second half follows רבנן

steps.title: אביי also split the ברייתא this way
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהא of בי כתיל tells רב אשי that אביי said the same thing: first half רבי שמעון, second half רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהא of בי כתיל said to רב אשי: This is what אביי said: the first clause follows רבי שמעון and the latter clause follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The surprising split is backed up by a tradition from אביי. He also read the ברייתא as half רבי שמעון and half רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer looked stretched, but now it is supported by an earlier אמורא. This shows that the split was not made up only to escape a problem. אביי had already read the ברייתא this way.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Like this; in this way

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the lost חטאת is split: the first half follows רבי שמעון and the second half follows רבנן. אביי confirms this reading.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב גְּבִיהָא דְּבֵי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Geviha of Bei Katil said to Rav Ashi:
This is what Abaye said:
The first clause follows Rabbi Shimon
and the latter clause follows the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גְּבִיהָא דְּבֵי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the split reading from step 1 with a tradition from אביי
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא is split between רבי שמעון and רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition of אביי, passed on by רב גביהא of בי כתיל to רב אשי

steps.title: No מעילה for impure קדשי קדשים meat or burned אימורין
steps.stepSummary: רבא says all agree that there is no liability for benefiting from impure meat of קדשי קדשים before זריקה, or from the אימורין of קדשים קלים after they were placed on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: All agree that if one benefited from meat of most-sacred offerings that became impure before the sprinkling of the blood, or from the sacrificial parts of lesser-sanctity offerings after they were brought up on the altar, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states a new rule that all sides agree to. Someone who benefits from these two kinds of sacrificial items is פטור from מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases nothing useful is left to do with the item except burn it. The impure meat can't be eaten or offered. The אימורין are already on the altar. Because of this, they no longer count as Temple property in a way that could bring מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Benefited from (the act that can cause מְעִילָה)
Offerings of the most sacred level
Sprinkling the blood on the altar
Fats and parts of a קׇרְבָּן that are burned on the altar
Offerings of lesser holiness

phrases.english: Rava says: All agree
phrases.notes: "All" means both sides of the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן on the previous amud.

phrases.english: that if one benefited from the meat of most-sacred offerings
that became impure before the sprinkling of the blood,
or from the sacrificial parts of lesser-sanctity offerings
after he brought them up on the altar, that he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the ברייתא discussion is closed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no מעילה for benefiting from impure קדשי קדשים meat before זריקה, or from אימורי קדשים קלים after they were placed on the altar

steps.title: Isn't that obvious? No loss was caused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this. The person who benefited caused no loss to the הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! What loss is he causing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule as too obvious to need saying. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה is about harming or using up holy property. Here the items are useless for any Temple purpose anyway, so it seems clear there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; so why say it?
What is he causing to be lost?

phrases.english: It is obvious! What loss is he causing?
phrases.notes: Impure meat can't be eaten or offered, and the fats are already on the altar. So nothing is lost by his benefiting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's statement teaches anything new
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the items have no remaining use for the הקדש, no loss is caused. So the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: The מצוה to burn or turn them doesn't create מעילה
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that the מצוה for the כהנים to burn impure meat, and the מצוה to turn the fats on the altar with a fork, keep these items holy enough for מעילה. רבא teaches that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: impure meat of most-sacred offerings has a מצוה of burning for the priests, and the sacrificial parts of lesser-sanctity offerings have a מצוה to turn them over with a fork. So he teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's rule is not obvious. There is still a מצוה left to do with each item, and we might have thought that makes it count for מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חידוש is that a leftover מצוה, like burning or turning the fats, does not make the item count as active holy property for מעילה. Having a מצוה to do with the item is not enough. A later piece of the עבודה is what would matter, and these acts do not count as that.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
The commandment to burn (disqualified holy meat)
To turn over
A fork or hook used on the altar
He teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: A leftover מצוה like burning impure meat, or turning the fats on the altar, does not make an item subject to מעילה. Someone who benefits from it is פטור.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the meat or fats stop being holy. They still must be burned. The point is only that benefiting from them does not bring the penalty of מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that liability for מעילה depends on whether the item still has a real role in the Temple service. Just having a related מצוה is not enough.

phrases.english: You might have said
the meat of most-sacred offerings that became impure
has a מצוה of burning for the priests,
and the sacrificial parts of lesser-sanctity offerings
have a מצוה to turn them over with a fork,
phrases.notes: "Them" is the fats on the altar fire, turned so they burn well.

phrases.english: so he teaches us that it is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by showing what mistake רבא's rule prevents
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the חידוש by naming a likely mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The remaining מצוה of burning or turning would make the items subject to מעילה
steps.terutzMaskana: These מצוות do not create liability for מעילה, so he is פטור

steps.title: רבא limits when the money goes to the Dead Sea
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא's ruling (money goes to ים המלח) applies only if he found out before the כפרה. If he found out after, the money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The ruling you quoted, 'if the חטאת was already brought, the money goes to ים המלח,' applies when he found out before the atonement. But if he found out only after the atonement, the money goes toward voluntary offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to an earlier ruling. The money is thrown into ים המלח only if the person learned about his מעילה before his חטאת was brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling covered someone whose חטאת was already offered: his leftover money goes to ים המלח. רבא splits this into two cases. If he knew before the כפרה, the ruling stands. If he only learned after the כפרה, the money goes to נדבה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The Dead Sea. Money 'sent' there is destroyed so that no one can benefit from it.
Atonement. Here it means the moment the חטאת is offered.
Voluntary offerings bought for the מזבח with leftover money.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This ruling that you stated,
"if the sin offering was already brought,
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from the previous amud, about money owed for using הקדש.

phrases.english: the money should go to the Dead Sea"
applies only when it became known to him
before the atonement.
But if he found out after the atonement,
the money goes toward voluntary offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement of רבא that narrows the scope of an earlier ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The money goes to ים המלח only if he learned of the מעילה before the כפרה. If he learned after, it goes to נדבה.

steps.title: The reason: we never set money aside to be destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's ruling: we do not set money aside from the start for it to be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? We do not set something aside from the start in order for it to be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters when he found out, and answers with a general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he only learned about the מעילה after his כפרה, then whatever money he now sets aside was never meant for a חטאת. Sending it to ים המלח would mean setting it aside just to destroy it, and the rule is that we don't do that. So it goes to נדבה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not set something aside for it to be destroyed.
From the start, at the moment it is first set aside.

steps.whatToRemember: Money goes to ים המלח only if it was first set aside while it still had a real purpose. We never set money aside just to throw it away.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
We do not set something aside from the start in order for it to be destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אֵין מַפְרִישִׁין מִתְּחִלָּה לְאִיבּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבא's distinction in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does finding out after the כפרה change where the money goes?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because we never set money aside from the start for it to be destroyed.

steps.title: משנה: items burned entirely on the altar are subject to misuse from consecration
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, מנחת כהנים, מנחת כהן משיח, and מנחת נסכים. מעילה applies to all of them from the moment they are made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעילה applies to the קומץ, the לבונה, the קטורת, the מנחה of כהנים, the מנחה of the כהן משיח, and the מנחה brought with נסכים, from the moment they were made holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists items that go completely to the מזבח and says מעילה applies to them right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קרבנות that the כהנים eat, מעילה can stop at some point (as in the earlier steps). None of these items are eaten by anyone. They belong entirely to the מזבח, so מעילה applies from the moment they are declared holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח.
Frankincense burned with the קומץ.
The incense burned daily on the golden מזבח.
The anointed כהן, meaning the כהן גדול.
The flour offering brought along with the wine poured for a קרבן.
One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of הקדש.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The handful, the frankincense, and the incense,
the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the meal offering of libations:
one is liable for misuse of them from when they were consecrated.
phrases.notes: This means from the moment they were declared holy, even before they were put into a holy vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items that go entirely to the מזבח are subject to מעילה from the moment they are made holy.

steps.title: Once placed in a vessel: disqualifications and prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: Once these items are placed in a כלי שרת, they can become פסול through a טבול יום, a מחוסר כפורים, or לינה. One is liable for נותר and טמא, but פיגול does not apply to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he made them holy in a vessel, they can become disqualified by a טבול יום, by a מחוסר כפורים, and by being left overnight. One is liable for them because of נותר and because of eating while טמא, but פיגול does not apply to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a second stage: being placed in a holy vessel. It lists what can now make these items unfit and which prohibitions apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being declared holy is enough for מעילה. Being placed in a כלי שרת is a stronger holiness, and only then can the item become פסול in these ways. The prohibitions of נותר and טמא apply, but פיגול does not. Steps 10-11 explain why: these items have no מתירין.

keyTerms.meaning: Making something holy by placing it in a כלי שרת, a holy service vessel.
Someone who immersed today but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור.
Someone who is טהור but still needs to bring his atonement offering.
Being left overnight, which makes it פסול.
Holy food left past its time limit.
An offering made unfit by the wrong intention about when it would be eaten or burned.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate stages here. Being declared holy (step 8) is enough for מעילה. Being placed in a vessel (this step) is what makes the item able to become פסול.

phrases.english: Once he consecrated them in a vessel,
it became able to be disqualified by one who immersed that day,
by one lacking atonement, and by being left overnight,
and one is liable for it because of notar,
and because of eating it while impure,
but piggul does not apply to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִדְּשָׁן בִּכְלִי – הוּכְשַׁר לִיפָּסֵל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from being declared holy to being made holy in a vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once placed in a vessel, these items can become פסול through a טבול יום, a מחוסר כפורים, or לינה. One is liable for נותר and טמא, but not for פיגול.

steps.title: The general rule about permitting factors
steps.stepSummary: Anything that has מתירין: one is not liable for פיגול, נותר, or טמא until the מתירין are offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anything that has permitting factors, one is not liable for it because of פיגול, נותר, or טמא until the permitting factors are offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a general rule about when the prohibitions of פיגול, נותר, and טמא begin for items that are permitted by something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some items become permitted only after something else is offered, such as the meat of a קרבן after the blood is sprinkled. For these items, liability for פיגול, נותר, and טמא waits until that permitting item is offered. The items in our משנה are burned completely and have no other permitting item, which helps explain why step 9 treated them differently.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule.
Permitting factors: the part of the service that makes something else permitted to the מזבח or to people.

steps.whatToRemember: Stage 1: מעילה applies from the moment the item is declared holy. Stage 2: placing it in a vessel makes it able to become פסול. For items that have מתירין, liability for פיגול, נותר, and טמא begins only after the מתירין are offered.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מתירין is a basic tool across קדשים. It decides when the strict penalties for misusing an offering begin.

phrases.english: This is the general rule:
anything that has permitting factors,
one is not liable for it
because of piggul, notar, or impurity
until the permitting factors are offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the משנה with a general rule that relates to the prohibitions listed in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For anything that has מתירין, liability for פיגול, נותר, and טמא begins only once the מתירין have been offered.

steps.title: Items without permitting factors: liable once placed in the vessel, but no פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that anything with no מתירין becomes subject to נותר and טמא once it is made holy in a כלי שרת, but פיגול does not apply to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything that has no מתירין: once it was made holy in a כלי שרת, one is liable for it because of נותר and טמא, but פיגול does not apply to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second half of its general rule. It now covers items that have no מתירין, the opposite of the case in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some items, like the קומץ and לבונה, are themselves the thing that permits other parts of the offering. Nothing else has to be offered to permit them. So there is nothing to wait for: the moment they are made holy in a כלי שרת, the laws of נותר and טמא apply. But פיגול only applies to something that has מתירין, so it never applies to these items.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating sacred food while ritually impure, which also brings כרת

steps.whatToRemember: Two mirror rules: if an item HAS מתירין, liability for פיגול, נותר, and טמא starts only after the מתירין are offered. If an item has NO מתירין, liability for נותר and טמא starts as soon as it is placed in a כלי שרת, and פיגול never applies.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that items without מתירין are less strict. They become subject to נותר and טמא earlier, right when they enter the vessel. The only thing missing is פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains the list from steps 8-9 (קומץ, לבונה, קטורת, and the מנחות): they are all items with no מתירין, which is why פיגול does not apply to them.

phrases.english: And anything that does not have permitting factors,
phrases.notes: For example the קומץ and לבונה: they permit other things, but nothing else has to be offered to permit them.

phrases.english: once one made it holy in the vessel,
one is liable for it because of leftover and impurity,
but פיגול does not apply to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror case of step 10: step 10 covered items WITH מתירין; this step covers items WITHOUT מתירין and explains the rule from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items without מתירין: liability for נותר and טמא begins once they are made holy in a כלי שרת; פיגול does not apply.
